learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the beautiful balance of nature and math by finding perfect mirror reflections hidden in shapes!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: If you can fold a picture perfectly in half so that both sides match exactly, that picture has symmetry! The crease where you folded the paper is called the line of symmetry.
Symmetry is not just in math books; it is everywhere! Look at a butterfly's wings, a human face, or a beautiful leaf. Nature loves to keep things balanced and perfectly matched on both sides.

fun_activity.title: 🎨 The Inkblot Monster
fun_activity.instructions: Take a piece of paper and fold it in half. Open it up, put a few drops of wet paint right on the crease, and fold it closed again. Press down smoothly, then open it to reveal your perfectly symmetrical inkblot monster!

quick_recap: ⭐ A shape has symmetry if one half is a perfect mirror image of the other half.
⭐ The imaginary line dividing the shape into matching halves is the axis of symmetry.
⭐ Some shapes, like a circle or a square, can have multiple lines of symmetry!
